title: Command Palette doesn't open when an elevated application is in focus
author: grallbring

status.label: Duplicate known limitation
status.detail: The elevated-foreground activation failure is already tracked in #39704; #45126 was closed as a duplicate after maintainers documented the integrity-level limitation.

next_action.label: Post duplicate response
next_action.reason: Acknowledge the privacy concern and consolidate the known elevation behavior under #39704 without requesting public diagnostics.

judgment.rationale: The reported elevated-foreground scenario is covered by open issue #39704. Maintainers closed #45126 as its duplicate after documenting that supporting this path requires elevated hook handling outside Command Palette's current stack.
evidence: The reporter reproduced on Windows 11 25H2 with multiple shortcuts and with the low-level hook both enabled and disabled.
The reporter explicitly declined to upload a diagnostic archive because of system-information privacy concerns.
Maintainers explained in #45126 that an unelevated CmdPal low-level hook does not receive input from elevated foreground applications; #45126 was closed as a duplicate of #39704.
judgment.recommended_action: Post a respectful consolidation response linking #39704 and do not ask the reporter to publish a diagnostic archive.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette does not activate while an elevated application owns focus, despite testing alternate shortcuts and the low-level-hook setting. The reporter prefers not to publish a diagnostic archive because of its system-information content.
known_information: PowerToys 0.100.2 was installed from the Microsoft Store on Windows 11 25H2.
The behavior occurs with elevated applications in focus and persists with a non-Windows-key shortcut.
The low-level keyboard hook setting did not change the result.
Open issue #39704 tracks Command Palette activation against elevated foreground applications, and #45126 was closed as its duplicate.
inferences: The matching scenario and the prior maintainer explanation make the same integration limitation likely; this issue alone does not establish implementation details for every process involved.
issue_context.analysis: The live report supplies the decision-relevant scenario and the linked work already owns it. Asking for public diagnostics would not change consolidation, especially after the reporter raised a privacy concern.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body, reporter follow-up, labels, and timeline.
Verified that #39704 remains open and that #45126 was explicitly closed as a duplicate of #39704 after a maintainer described the elevated-hook integration constraint.
Verified that #50109 is a different open Command Palette shortcut problem involving the Settings window.

actions.label: Post duplicate response

comment.body: Thanks for testing multiple shortcuts and both low-level-hook settings. Your concern about publishing a diagnostic archive is understandable, and no public ZIP is needed for this triage decision. The elevated-foreground activation limitation is already tracked in #39704. The same Task Manager/elevation scenario was investigated in #45126, which was closed as a duplicate of #39704 after maintainers documented the integration constraint. Please add any further impact or requirements to #39704 so the work stays consolidated.
